profile_text.body:
Snowflake is a for-profit, publicly traded company (NYSE: SNOW) founded in 2012 and headquartered in Bozeman, MT. Its site describes it as operating an "AI Data Cloud" that covers data ingestion, processing, analysis, modeling, and the building and sharing of data and AI applications. The company positions its platform as eliminating data silos and enabling organizations to collaborate and build AI-powered applications within a single, secure, and scalable environment. The site also notes the availability of Snowflake Postgres, described as bringing a popular database engine into the AI Data Cloud without requiring complex data pipelines.

On the AI product side, Snowflake offers Snowflake Arctic, an enterprise-focused large language model released under the Apache 2.0 license with integration into the data cloud for commercial use, and Snowflake Cortex, a native AI layer within the data cloud that provides LLM functions, vector search, data residency controls, and governance through Snowflake Horizon. The site references customer deployments at Under Armour, Booking.com, and Landing AI, the last of which uses Snowflake alongside AWS as a foundation for AI product development with attention to data governance concerns.

Snowflake's most recently reported annual revenue, drawn from a 10-K filing for the period ending January 31, 2026, was $4,683,946,000. The company trades under the ticker SNOW and carries SEC CIK 0001640147. No litigation or MCP server registrations are recorded in the held facts.
